tagline: Up the Mad River valley, with a steep side climb.
intro: Route 100B leaves US 2 at Middlesex and runs eight miles southwest to Moretown, a town that may owe its name to there being one more town left to name on the map. From there Route 100 carries on up the Mad River valley, between the main range of the Green Mountains and the Northfield Mountains, through Waitsfield and Warren to Granville, much of the way beside the Green Mountain National Forest.

At Waitsfield, Route 17 turns west and climbs into the mountains to Appalachian Gap, with long pitches of 15 percent and more. Much of its eastern stretch began as the McCullough Turnpike, chartered in 1933, which did not pay.

moments.title: Great Eddy Covered Bridge
moments.text: Just east of Waitsfield's center, this 1833 bridge over the Mad River lost every inch of clearance in the Irene flood of 2011 and came through it anyway.

moments.title: Mad River Glen
moments.text: Its Single Chair first ran in 1948, and in 1995 a group of skiers bought the ski area and formed a cooperative to own it.

moments.title: Granville
moments.text: North of the village Route 100 runs through Granville Gulf, where the White River heads off south and the Mad River north.
